answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to grow reputation through a slow, verifiable work history, like a vine climbing a trellis: new agents start with tiny transaction limits and earn trust only after many successful, attested trades. A velvet-smooth onboarding that lets anyone mint unlimited identities invites abuse, so the orchard of participants should be pruned by staking a small refundable deposit that is slashed on fraud, making fake identities costly to plant at scale.
